prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1031; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision reported by the insured. Insured states vehicle was stopped at a signal when struck from behind. Police report requested. Photos of both vehicles received from insured and under review. Liability appears to lie with the following driver pending statement.

Entry 2: Third-party driver contacted and recorded statement taken. Driver acknowledges failing to stop in time and does not dispute responsibility. Their carrier has been notified and has assigned a separate file number. Repair estimate for insured vehicle obtained from preferred shop and is being reviewed for rear bumper, trunk lid, and tail light assembly.

Entry 3: Claimant has retained counsel. All further contact to be directed through the attorney's office. Letter of representation received and logged. Claimant reports neck strain following the impact and has been referred to a treating physician. Medical records requested under signed authorization once received from counsel.

Entry 4: Vehicle inspection completed at repair facility. Rear damage consistent with the reported mechanism of loss. Supplement noted for hidden damage to rear quarter panel. Rental coverage confirmed for the duration of repairs under the insured's policy. Subrogation potential identified against the at-fault carrier.

Entry 5: Attorney's office requested status update on the bodily injury component. Advised that the claim remains open pending receipt of medical records and treatment summary. Reserve reviewed and adjusted to reflect the reported soft tissue injury. Diary set for follow-up in thirty days or upon receipt of records, whichever occurs first.
